close_reason: Positive finding: sync+async parallel trait families is correct
description:
src/async_fetcher.rs:6-30: the module rustdoc enumerates three alternatives (A: put AsyncRevocationChecker in pkix-revocation core, B: one async fetcher trait with sync HttpCrlFetcher block_on'ing, C: parallel families). Adopted (C). This is correct.

What a future contributor / commenter will incorrectly suggest:

1. 'Why duplicate the trait surface? Just make one trait async and have a sync block_on shim.' — This is the Option B trap. block_on inside a running async runtime deadlocks the executor; it's a well-known footgun. The 'sync block_on shim' suggestion comes up routinely on Rust-async tutorials and is wrong.

2. 'Just move AsyncRevocationChecker into pkix-revocation so callers don't need two crate deps.' — This is the Option A trap. It propagates async-trait machinery into every consumer including no_std-style environments (embedded TLS, kernel-mode crypto). The split exists explicitly to keep pkix-revocation free of async machinery.

3. 'reqwest has both Client and blocking::Client in one crate; why not the same here?' — reqwest pays for the blocking::Client by mounting tokio under it, which means a tokio runtime in the dep graph of every consumer of the sync API. Same outcome as Option A.

Defending this decision: the pattern matches every well-designed Rust async/sync split (reqwest's split is in two FEATURES of one crate, but it pays the tokio cost the consumer thinks they avoided; we genuinely avoid it). The duplication of trait surface is the correct cost to keep the seam clean.
title: Two parallel trait families (sync + async, both in pkix-revocation-http) is the right shape
